bib.title: CodeT5+: Open Code Large Language Models for Code Understanding and Generation

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only for lineage; figures 6-9 are images (captions only).

question: Can one family of encoder-decoder code LLMs, pretrained with a mixture of objectives and scaled by freezing off-the-shelf decoders, serve code understanding, generation and completion tasks better than single-architecture or single-objective code models?
hypothesis: Architecture inflexibility (encoder-only, decoder-only or one unified encoder-decoder for all tasks) and a limited set of pretraining objectives cause suboptimal performance on some tasks; a modular encoder-decoder with a mixed objective set closes the pretrain-finetune gap.
contributions: A family of encoder-decoder code LLMs (220M to 16B) whose encoder, decoder or both can be activated per task (encoder-only, decoder-only, encoder-decoder).
A two-stage pretraining mixture: span denoising and two causal-LM variants on unimodal code, then text-code contrastive, matching and causal-LM on bimodal data.
A compute-efficient scaling scheme: initialise a shallow encoder and deep decoder from CodeGen-mono, freeze the decoder, train only the encoder and one cross-attention layer.
Instruction tuning on about 20k synthetic code instructions (InstructCodeT5+).
Evaluation on 20+ benchmarks in zero-shot, finetuning and instruction-tuning settings, including a unified retrieval-augmented generation setting.

method.summary: CodeT5+ is a family of encoder-decoder code models. The 220M and 770M models are T5-base/large-shaped and pretrained from scratch in two stages (unimodal code, then bimodal CodeSearchNet text-code). The 2B, 6B and 16B models initialise the decoder from frozen CodeGen-mono and the encoder from CodeGen-mono 350M, connected by one new cross-attention layer; only the encoder and cross-attention train. Instruction tuning gives InstructCodeT5+.
method.task: code pretraining; zero-shot code generation (HumanEval); math programming; code summarization; line-level completion; text-to-code retrieval; defect and clone detection; retrieval-augmented code generation

datasets.name: Unimodal code (stage 1), from GitHub Code dataset (codeparrot/github-code)
datasets.size: 51.5B tokens (CodeT5 tokenizer), about 50x CodeSearchNet; 37,274,876 files across 9 languages
datasets.source: GitHub Code on HuggingFace, permissive licences only (mit, apache-2, bsd-3-clause, bsd-2-clause, cc0-1.0, unlicense, isc)
datasets.preprocessing: 9 languages (Python, Java, Ruby, JavaScript, Go, PHP, C, C++, C#); files of 50 to 2000 tokens; overlap with CodeSearchNet and downstream tasks removed by GitHub repository name; exact-match deduplicated version (ignoring whitespace), some duplicates may remain. Per-language file counts in Table 1 (Ruby 2,119,741; JS 5,856,984; Go 1,501,673; Python 3,418,376; Java 10,851,759; PHP 4,386,876; C 4,187,467; C++ 2,951,945; C# 4,119,796).

datasets.source: Husain et al. 2019; only the bimodal subset is used (CodeT5 used unimodal and bimodal)
datasets.preprocessing: Table 1 per-language: Ruby 49,009; JS 125,166; Go 319,132; Python 453,772; Java 457,381; PHP 525,357

models.name: CodeT5+ 2B / 6B / 16B
models.architecture: shallow encoder, deep decoder, cross-attention connecting them; decoder frozen
models.init_from: decoder from CodeGen-mono 2B/6B/16B, encoder from CodeGen-mono 350M

other.cross_attention: randomly initialised, inserted only in the top L=1 decoder layers
other.extra_trainable_params: 350M encoder plus one cross-attention layer of 36M, 67M, 151M for 2B, 6B, 16B
other.decoder_only_mode: freezes encoder and cross-attention, activates about half of total parameters

models.name: Baselines (RoBERTa, CodeBERT, GraphCodeBERT, SYNCOBERT, UniXcoder, GPT-2, CodeGPT, PaLM, GPT-4, Codex, LLaMA, CodeGen, InCoder, GPT-J, GPT-Neo, GPT-NeoX, MIM, CodeGeeX, Replit, StarCoder, PLBART, CodeT5, LaMDA, AlphaCode, Minerva, REDCODER-EXT, SCODE-R)

other.note: most baseline numbers copied from prior papers; not stated which were rerun

training.objective: Stage 1 (unimodal): span denoising (15% of tokens masked, whole-word, mean span length 3, uniform) then two causal-LM variants (seq2seq with pivot uniformly sampled between 10% and 90%; decoder-only with [CLM] token to encoder), equal weights. Stage 2 (bimodal): text-code contrastive + matching + two causal-LM losses (text-to-code, code-to-text), equal weights, L = Ltcc + Ltcm + Lt2c + Lc2t (Appendix B Eq. 5).
training.warmup: stage 1: 10k steps of span denoising only, then joint training with the two CLM tasks
training.batch_size: stage 1: 2048 for denoising, 512 for CLM; stage 2: 256
training.epochs: stage 2: 10 epochs; instruction tuning: up to 3 epochs; HumanEval adaptation: one more epoch on Python subset with causal LM
training.tokens: 51.5B tokens in the unimodal corpus (tokens seen not stated)
training.seq_len: stage 1: 512 (denoising); 768 source / 600 target (seq2seq CLM); 1 source / 1024 target (decoder-only CLM). Stage 2: 420 code, 128 text.
training.precision: DeepSpeed ZeRO stage 2, FP16 mixed precision; for 2B/6B/16B frozen decoder in FP16, other trainable weights FP32; ZeRO stage 3 parameter partition for 6B and 16B
training.hardware: cluster of 16 A100-40G GPUs on Google Cloud Platform

other.contrastive: 256-d L2-normalised [CLS] embeddings, momentum encoder with queue, learned temperature; matching uses hard negatives mined from the queue
other.finetune_retrieval: max len 350 code / 64 text, lr 2e-5, 10 epochs, 8 A100, batch 64, queues of size 57600, 64 hard negatives
other.finetune_summarization: max len 256 source / 128 target, lr 2e-5, batch 64, 10 epochs
other.finetune_completion: lr 2e-5, batch 32, decoder max len 1024, 30 epochs
other.finetune_rag: max len 600 source / 320 target, lr 2e-5, batch 32, 10 epochs

inference.decoding: HumanEval: nucleus sampling. Summarization, completion, RAG, math pass@1: beam search, beam size 5. Math pass@80 and pass@100: nucleus sampling.
inference.temperature: HumanEval 0.2, 0.6, 0.8 for k=1, 10, 100; math pass@80/100 temperature 1.2
inference.top_p: 0.95 for math pass@80/100; HumanEval top-p not stated
inference.samples: pass@k with k generated programs per problem; number of samples n used for the pass@k estimator not stated; single run, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot for HumanEval and InstructCodeT5+; CodeT setting: model prompted with an assert statement to generate extra test cases, which filter candidate programs
inference.retrieval: encoder embeds code snippets (256-d), faiss index, L-2 similarity, top-k = 1 in main result; retrieved code joined by [SEP] and appended to source; docstrings not appended; target string excluded from retrieved set

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: percentage of problems solved using k generated programs (unit tests for HumanEval; execution output for math)

metrics.name: smoothed BLEU-4
metrics.definition: token-based similarity between predicted and reference summaries

metrics.name: Exact Match and Levenshtein edit similarity
MRR
metrics.definition: mean reciprocal rank in text-to-code retrieval

baselines: see models list: closed- and open-source decoder-only LLMs on HumanEval; encoder-only, decoder-only (CodeGen-multi 350M, CodeGPT), encoder-decoder (PLBART, CodeT5) for finetuned tasks; REDCODER-EXT for RAG
eval.protocol: Single reported numbers, no seeds, no confidence intervals or significance tests. Baselines in zero-shot HumanEval include closed models whose sizes are not disclosed. The authors note that Codex and CodeGen training data was not decontaminated against the downstream tasks, so comparisons on summarization and completion are not clean.

evidence.quote: the 350M encoder plus one cross-attention layer of 36M, 67M, 151M for 2B, 6B, 16B models respectively
We employ nucleus sampling with a temperature of 1.2 and top-p=0.95.

results.claim: Instruction-tuned CodeT5+ 16B reaches 35.0% pass@1 on zero-shot HumanEval, the best among open code LLMs in that comparison (StarCoder 15B scores 33.6) and above code-cushman-001 (33.5).
results.setup: HumanEval 164 problems, zero-shot, InstructCodeT5+ 16B, nucleus sampling temperature 0.2 for k=1; model first adapted with one more epoch of causal LM on Python data.
results.quote: achieving new SoTA of 35.0% pass@1 and 54.5% pass@10
results.note: StarCoder (prompted) 15B scores 40.8 pass@1 in the same table's generation-strategy block, above InstructCodeT5+ without CodeT.

results.claim: With CodeT-style generated-test filtering, InstructCodeT5+ 16B reaches 42.9% pass@1 and 67.8% pass@10.
results.baseline_value: 36.7 CodeGen-mono 16B w/ CodeT; 38.5 CodeT5+ 16B w/ CodeT
results.setup: HumanEval zero-shot, InstructCodeT5+ 16B, model generates test cases from an assert prompt which filter and rank samples.
results.quote: achieving up to 42.9% pass@1 and 67.8% pass@10

results.claim: Small CodeT5+ models match much larger code LLMs on HumanEval: 770M scores 15.5% pass@1 against InCoder 6B 15.2, GPT-NeoX 20B 15.4 and PaLM 62B 15.9.
results.setup: HumanEval zero-shot, CodeT5+ 770M, trained from scratch; baseline numbers are as listed in Table 2.

results.claim: The frozen-decoder CodeT5+ models beat same-size CodeGen-mono on HumanEval pass@1 at 2B (24.2 vs 23.7), 6B (28.0 vs 26.1) and 16B (30.9 vs 29.3).
results.setup: HumanEval zero-shot, CodeT5+ 16B (frozen CodeGen-mono 16B decoder) vs CodeGen-mono 16B; CodeT5+ received an additional Python-subset epoch.
results.table: Table 2, rows CodeT5+ 16B and CodeGen-mono 16B, column pass@1
results.note: The comparison also differs in an extra epoch of Python causal-LM pretraining for CodeT5+, following Nijkamp et al.

results.claim: CodeT5+ 770M fine-tuned reaches 87.4 pass@80 on MathQA-Python, a new SoTA.
results.setup: MathQA-Python test, finetuned 30 epochs, lr 2e-5, pass@80 with nucleus sampling temperature 1.2, top-p 0.95.
results.quote: our CodeT5+ 770M achieves new SoTA results of 87.4 pass@80 on MathQA-Python

results.claim: CodeT5+ 770M reaches 73.8 pass@100 on GSM8K-Python after finetuning, below Minerva 540B (78.5, few-shot with majority voting) and above LLaMA 65B (69.7) and code-davinci (71.0).
results.setup: GSM8K-Python (5,861 converted training samples, 1,000 test), finetuned, nucleus sampling temperature 1.2 top-p 0.95. Baseline rows mix few-shot and finetuned settings and some use majority voting or self-sampling optimisation.
results.quote: very competitive results of 73.8 pass@100 on GSM8K-Python

results.claim: On line-level completion, decoder-only CodeT5+ 220M beats CodeT5 220M by 6.5 EM on PY150 and 10.4 EM on JavaCorpus; the authors attribute this to the stage-1 causal-LM objectives.
results.setup: PY150 and JavaCorpus (CodeXGLUE), CodeT5+ used in decoder-only mode (about half the parameters active), finetuned 30 epochs, beam 5.

results.claim: CodeT5+ 770M reaches 44.86 EM on PY150 and 37.90 EM on JavaCorpus, a new SoTA over CodeGen-multi 350M (42.47, 35.47) and UniXcoder 125M (43.12, 32.90).
results.setup: PY150 line-level completion, finetuned, decoder-only mode.
results.table: Table 5, row CodeT5+ 770M, column PY150 EM
results.note: Authors concede CodeGen-multi 350M may have data leakage from pretraining.

results.claim: Removing the stage-1 causal-LM objective drops CodeT5+ 770M PY150 EM from 44.9 to 36.2 and JavaCorpus EM from 37.9 to 24.8.
results.setup: Ablation on CodeT5+ 770M, finetuned PY150 line-level completion; same ablation row also lowers MathQA-PY pass@80 87.4 to 72.3 and GSM8K-PY pass@100 73.8 to 61.4.
results.table: Table 7, row a) no causal LM, column PY150 EM

results.claim: CodeT5+ 770M obtains 77.4 overall MRR on CodeSearchNet text-to-code retrieval across six languages, against UniXcoder 125M at 74.4; 220M gets 77.1.
results.setup: CodeSearchNet filtered (CodeXGLUE), finetuned 10 epochs lr 2e-5; both encoder AND decoder of CodeT5+ activated (encoder embeddings plus decoder matching head), MRR.
results.quote: In this task, we activate both encoder and decoder of CodeT5+
results.table: Table 6, row CodeT5+ 770M, column Overall (CSN) 77.4; row UniXcoder 125M 74.4
results.note: Text says the 770M model surpasses UniXcoder by more than 3 absolute MRR points on all 3 tasks across 8 datasets; Table 6 lists 7 CSN/Adv columns plus CosQA.

results.claim: Removing the text-code matching objective in stage 2 costs 2.6 average MRR over the six CSN languages (77.4 to 74.8).
results.setup: Ablation on CodeT5+ 770M, text-to-code retrieval on CSN, six languages.
results.quote: a drop of 2.6 avg. MRR over 6
results.note: Removing the causal LM objective in stage 2 costs 0.6 (76.8).

results.claim: As a unified retriever-generator, CodeT5+ 220M with top-1 retrieval beats REDCODER-EXT (top-10) on Java and Python code generation: BLEU-4 33.83 vs 28.98 and 31.14 vs 24.43.
results.metric: BLEU-4 gain, avg of two languages
results.setup: CodeXGLUE Java and Python code generation following Parvez et al. 2021, finetuned 10 epochs, beam 5, top-1 retrieval, code snippets only (no docstrings).
results.quote: 2 retrieval-augmented code generation tasks (+5.8 avg. BLEU-4)
results.note: Table 8 EM is 11.66 Java and 11.83 Python vs 10.21 and 9.61.

results.claim: Retrieval-augmented performance saturates at k=5 retrieved snippets, which the authors attribute to the 600-token source length.
results.setup: CodeT5+ 220M, Java and Python RAG generation, Table 10.
results.note: BLEU-4 actually peaks at top-1 (33.83 Java, 31.14 Python) and falls with larger k; EM and CodeBLEU peak at k=5.

results.claim: CodeT5+ 770M improves code summarization overall BLEU-4 to 20.15 against CodeT5 220M 19.55 and UniXcoder 19.30.
results.setup: CodeSearchNet clean, six languages, finetuned 10 epochs, beam 5.
results.note: Authors write that summarization and retrieval gains saturate with model size.

results.claim: CodeT5+ 770M reaches 66.7% accuracy on defect detection; clone detection F1 is about equal to baselines (95.1 vs 95.2).
results.setup: CodeXGLUE Devign (C functions) and BigCloneBench, finetuned 10 and 2 epochs.
results.quote: of 66.7% on the defect detection task

results.claim: Pretraining corpus: 51.5B tokens of permissively licensed code in 9 languages, about 50x CodeSearchNet.
results.setup: CodeT5 tokenizer, files 50 to 2000 tokens, overlap with downstream tasks removed by repo name.

results.claim: Scaling by freezing the decoder leaves few trainable parameters beyond the 350M encoder: one cross-attention layer of 36M, 67M, 151M for the 2B, 6B, 16B models.
results.setup: CodeT5+ 2B/6B/16B, L=1 cross-attention layer, frozen CodeGen-mono decoder.
results.quote: the 350M encoder plus one cross-attention layer of 36M, 67M, 151M for 2B,

results.claim: Hardware reported for pretraining is 16 A100-40G GPUs; wall-clock time and total GPU-hours are not given.
results.setup: Pretraining of all CodeT5+ sizes, Google Cloud Platform.
results.quote: a cluster with 16 A100-40G GPUs on Google Cloud Platform

limits: Authors state billion-parameter LLMs such as Codex and CodeGen use GitHub code without removing overlap with the downstream tasks, so fair comparison is difficult, especially for summarization and completion; CodeGen-multi 350M is kept despite potential leakage.
Authors note that for finetuned summarization and retrieval, gains saturate with model size.
Authors concede gaps against GPT-4 and code-davinci-002 and that their details are unknown; also a gap against Minerva on GSM8K-Python.
Instruction data is LM-generated and noisy (Fig 4 includes a wrong output).
Residual duplicates may remain in the pretraining data despite exact-match deduplication.
No seeds, variance, confidence intervals or significance tests; number of samples n for pass@k not stated; compute reported only as 16 A100-40G with no hours.
Model hidden size, layer count and heads for the from-scratch models are not given (only 'T5-base/large').
Infilling-style code completion with right context is out of scope.
The HumanEval 2B-16B comparison with CodeGen includes an extra Python epoch only for CodeT5+.
Dated: HumanEval comparisons are to 2023 models (StarCoder prompted 40.8 already exceeds it); the benchmark is now saturated.

terms.definition: an encoder-decoder with a small encoder and a large decoder, both initialised from pretrained checkpoints and joined by cross-attention layers; only the encoder and cross-attention are trained
a pivot location is sampled uniformly between 10% and 90% of the sequence; the context before it is the source and the sequence after it the target, with a [CLM] token prepended to the source
